foundations.name: Scalar numerics and Boolean
foundations.baseline: Core signed and unsigned integers, floats, casts, and Boolean rules exist.
foundations.completion: Define exact Arrow cast, overflow, comparison, NaN, and non-finite behavior.

foundations.name: Null values
foundations.baseline: The language has none and finite unions, and Arrow arrays expose validity metadata.
foundations.completion: Define nullable scalar semantics, validity propagation, equality, ordering, casts, and branch behavior.

foundations.name: Strings and bytes
foundations.owner: ASTx types, IRx analysis, and IRx native runtime
foundations.baseline: UTF-8 strings exist, and Arrow RecordBatch supports UTF-8 internally.
foundations.completion: Add owned and borrowed binary values, large offsets, Unicode conversion, view lifetimes, and zero-copy rules.

foundations.name: Decimal values
foundations.owner: ASTx types, Arx frontend, and IRx
foundations.baseline: ASTx reserves decimal data-type kinds but has no usable decimal value model.
foundations.completion: Add types and literals, precision and scale checks, 32/64/128/256-bit representation, arithmetic, casts, and ABI rules.

foundations.name: Temporal values
foundations.owner: ASTx types, Arx frontend, and IRx
foundations.baseline: Date, time, timestamp, and datetime types and literals exist.
foundations.completion: Add Arrow units, duration and interval types, timezone metadata, range checks, and conversion policy.

foundations.name: Parametric and structural types
foundations.baseline: Templates, tensors, DataFrames, structs, and unions provide partial foundations.
foundations.completion: Support recursive schema parameters, fixed sizes, dictionary types, union codes, field nullability, and canonical equality.

foundations.name: Compile-time values
foundations.baseline: Tensor dimensions and DataFrame fields carry selected static metadata.
foundations.completion: Provide checked type parameters for dimensions, decimal precision and scale, time units, fixed sizes, and schema fields.

foundations.name: Ownership and destruction
foundations.baseline: Strings and dynamic lists have semantic ownership. Native Arrow handles, including batches produced through irx_rb compatibility, now use checked shared or unique owner tokens, while IRx semantic ownership remains incomplete.
foundations.completion: Generalize ownership to handles, views, fields, calls, returns, temporaries, failures, classes, and generators.

foundations.name: Buffer and bitmap model
foundations.baseline: irx_buffer_view models data, owner, dtype, shape, strides, offset, and flags.
foundations.completion: Add checked bounds, validity bitmaps, variable-width offsets, alignment, endianness, and large-buffer overflow checks.

foundations.name: Collection sizes and indices
foundations.owner: IRx analysis, lowering, and native runtime
foundations.baseline: Existing APIs mix static metadata with several integer result widths.
foundations.completion: Standardize Arrow lengths, row counts, offsets, and indices on checked i64 semantics with explicit narrowing only.

foundations.name: Methods, overloads, and intrinsics
foundations.baseline: Typed calls and semantic sidecars exist without a canonical Arrow intrinsic registry.
foundations.completion: Add one typed builtin and intrinsic registry for containers and kernels that lowering consumes without re-resolution.

foundations.name: Error handling
foundations.owner: IRx analysis, lowering, and native runtime
foundations.baseline: The unified irx_arrow runtime uses fixed-width, Arx-owned status codes plus thread-local capture and immutable owned error snapshots. Deprecated irx_rb entry points preserve their integer results and translate failures from delegated unified operations.
foundations.completion: Implement recoverable/fatal propagation and failure cleanup across semantics, lowering, kernels, streams, and I/O.

foundations.name: Iteration and streaming
foundations.baseline: List iteration and initial generator support exist.
foundations.completion: Define Array and Series iteration, EOF, early close, cancellation, backpressure, and deterministic stream cleanup.

foundations.name: Classes and aggregate storage
foundations.baseline: Struct and class support exists, but general class destruction is incomplete.
foundations.completion: Add deterministic field destruction and move rules before aggregates may store owning Arrow handles.

foundations.name: FFI and opaque handles
foundations.baseline: C externs, version and feature queries, stable opaque handle kinds, checked owner-slot lifecycle operations, and cross-ABI RecordBatch C Data interchange exist.
foundations.completion: Add ownership and nullability annotations, complete C Data and C Stream contracts, and ABI conformance checks.

foundations.name: Modules, builtins, and standard library
foundations.baseline: Ambient builtins, bundled builtin modules, and a small standard library exist.
foundations.completion: Define stable intrinsic registration and public stdlib.compute, stdlib.io, and stdlib.dataset facades without an Arrow namespace.

foundations.name: Execution context
foundations.baseline: Runtime features declare typed transitive dependencies and automatically collect their native artifacts and linker flags during activation, but there is no Arrow execution-context value.
foundations.completion: Add memory pool, allocator, thread count, cancellation, resource limits, and optional device selection.

foundations.name: Native packaging
foundations.owner: IRx build, CI, and release tooling
foundations.baseline: Runtime sources build on demand from Arrow and PyArrow package metadata.
foundations.completion: Provide matched headers and libraries, platform discovery, clean-wheel execution, and cross-platform CI.

capabilities.name: Null and Boolean
capabilities.notes: Boolean arrays and validity metadata exist, but Arx has no unified nullable scalar semantics or three-valued compute rules.

evidence.purpose: Exercises explicit validity handling at the native array boundary.
Exercises null values in RecordBatch construction and access.

capabilities.name: Signed and unsigned integers and floats
capabilities.notes: Primitive array and scalar types exist, but Arrow-specific cast, overflow, and collection semantics are not complete end to end.

evidence.purpose: Round-trips every currently supported primitive type through Arrow C Data.

capabilities.name: Binary, large binary, and binary view
capabilities.notes: No general Arrow binary value, offsets, view lifetime, or Arx bytes surface is implemented.

evidence.purpose: Keeps this required Arrow 24 family explicit until conformance tests replace inventory-only evidence.

capabilities.name: UTF-8, large UTF-8, and string view
capabilities.notes: RecordBatch UTF-8 and large UTF-8 interoperate with PyArrow; general arrays, string views, DataFrame columns, and LLVM lowering do not.

evidence.purpose: Validates UTF-8 RecordBatch buffers through PyArrow.
Proves the general native Array boundary still rejects string arrays explicitly.

capabilities.name: Fixed-size binary
capabilities.notes: The fixed byte width is not represented in the type system or native ABI.

evidence.purpose: Keeps this required Arrow 24 family explicit until feature conformance exists.

capabilities.name: Decimal32, Decimal64, Decimal128, and Decimal256
capabilities.notes: ASTx reserves decimal data-type kinds, but precision, scale, values, semantics, ABI representation, and Arrow interoperability are absent.

evidence.purpose: Prevents reserved enum kinds from being reported as implemented decimal support.

capabilities.name: Date, time, timestamp, duration, and interval
capabilities.notes: RecordBatch date, time, and timestamp values work in Python; duration, intervals, complete unit metadata, timezone policy, and Arx-native containers remain incomplete.

evidence.purpose: Validates current native temporal RecordBatch buffers through PyArrow.
Checks one existing temporal overflow boundary.

capabilities.name: List, large list, fixed-size list, and list view
capabilities.notes: Ordinary Arx lists and fixed-width RecordBatch list children exist; recursive Arrow list schemas, large offsets, list views, and container lowering are incomplete.

evidence.purpose: Validates supported fixed-width list children through PyArrow.
Documents the current list child-type limitation.

capabilities.name: Struct and map
capabilities.notes: Fixed-width RecordBatch struct fields exist; recursive Arrow structs, maps, child ownership, and Arx container semantics do not.

evidence.purpose: Validates the supported RecordBatch struct representation through PyArrow.
Documents the current struct field-type limitation.

capabilities.name: Sparse and dense union
capabilities.notes: Arx type unions are not Arrow dense or sparse unions; type codes, offsets, storage, and interchange are not implemented.

evidence.purpose: Keeps Arrow unions distinct from existing language union types.

capabilities.name: Dictionary encoding
capabilities.notes: Index and value typing, ordered metadata, encode/decode operations, and interchange are absent.

evidence.purpose: Keeps this required Arrow 24 family explicit until feature conformance exists.

capabilities.name: Run-end encoded
capabilities.notes: Run-end and value child types, validation, decoding, and interchange are absent.

evidence.purpose: Keeps this required Arrow 24 family explicit until feature conformance exists.

capabilities.name: Extension types
capabilities.notes: The target is lossless storage and metadata preservation; execution will require separately registered extensions.

evidence.purpose: Tracks preserve-only scope without claiming executable extension semantics.

capabilities.name: Scalar and Buffer
capabilities.notes: IRx buffer views and owner retain/release exist, but first-class Arrow Scalar and Buffer value semantics are not exposed in Arx.

evidence.purpose: Exercises current native buffer owner lifetime operations.

capabilities.name: Array
capabilities.notes: Primitive native arrays and an internal int32 length node exist, but Array is not a general first-class Arx container.

evidence.purpose: Builds the primitive Array families implemented by the native runtime.
Covers the current internal Array length lowering helper.

capabilities.name: ChunkedArray and Series
capabilities.notes: DataFrame projection returns an opaque chunked-array-backed Series, but construction, iteration, methods, ownership, and interchange are incomplete.

evidence.purpose: Checks the existing Table column projection to a chunked array handle.

capabilities.name: RecordBatch
capabilities.notes: The deprecated Python/native irx_rb API supports selected types and IPC over the canonical shared RecordBatch handle. Stable irx_arrow retain, release, shape, and C Data interchange exist, but semantic analysis, lowering, and an Arx language value do not.

evidence.purpose: Exercises one RecordBatch through the current IPC stream API.
Keeps the transitional RecordBatch ABI version available during migration.
Proves legacy construction and access share the canonical handle, owner token, and C Data path.

capabilities.name: Table and DataFrame
capabilities.notes: Static numeric and Boolean DataFrames lower through Arrow Table handles; nullable, variable-width, nested, dynamic-schema, and interchange behavior is incomplete.

evidence.purpose: Checks current DataFrame literal lowering through the Arrow Table runtime.
Documents the current public DataFrame column-type limitation.

capabilities.name: Dense Tensor
capabilities.notes: Readonly fixed-width numeric dense tensors support shape, strides, views, and indexing; broader dtypes, mutation, conversion, and full interchange remain incomplete.

evidence.purpose: Checks compiler lowering through the Arrow dense Tensor owner bridge.
Checks native Tensor shape, strides, values, and borrowed owner lifetime.

capabilities.name: Sparse tensors
capabilities.notes: Sparse COO, CSR, CSC, and CSF types and validation are not implemented.

evidence.purpose: Keeps staged sparse tensor formats in the Arrow 24 inventory.

capabilities.name: Arrow C Data interface
capabilities.notes: Primitive arrays support import, export, copy, and move; variable-width, nested, dictionary, and other required Arrow types remain unsupported.

evidence.purpose: Exercises current native Arrow C Data export and import ownership.
Checks move import of an offset Array and adopted release callback.

capabilities.name: Arrow C Stream interface
capabilities.notes: A local C Stream struct declaration exists, but the ownership, EOF, cancellation, and general stream bridge are not implemented.

evidence.purpose: Prevents a declaration-only C Stream header from being treated as support.

capabilities.name: Compute kernels
capabilities.notes: Arx has scalar operators, but no typed Arrow kernel registry, options, execution context, native dispatch, or stdlib.compute facade.

evidence.purpose: Keeps Arrow Compute distinct from existing scalar operator lowering.

capabilities.name: IPC streams and files
capabilities.notes: The separate Python RecordBatch API reads and writes IPC streams and files; native Arx Stream and stdlib.io APIs do not exist.

evidence.purpose: Round-trips the current Python RecordBatch API through an IPC file.
Checks deterministic close behavior for the existing stream API.

capabilities.name: CSV, JSON, and Parquet
capabilities.notes: No stdlib.io readers, writers, option types, projection, pushdown, or native runtime features exist for these formats.

evidence.purpose: Keeps required file-format modules explicit until feature conformance exists.

capabilities.name: Filesystem, Dataset, and Scanner
capabilities.notes: Dataset expressions, scan builders, path and URI types, partitioning, streaming output, and stdlib.dataset are absent.

evidence.purpose: Keeps dataset execution in the staged Arrow 24 inventory.

capabilities.name: Acero execution plans
capabilities.notes: Typed plan nodes, schema propagation, execution ownership, cancellation, and bounded-memory behavior are absent.

evidence.purpose: Keeps Acero separate from a general-purpose query-language promise.

capabilities.name: Flight and Flight SQL
capabilities.notes: Flight remains an optional runtime feature so networking and RPC dependencies do not enter core programs.

evidence.purpose: Tracks Flight as optional rather than ambient core support.

capabilities.name: Substrait
capabilities.notes: Substrait import and export will be optional and must preserve unsupported extensions without weakening static checks.

evidence.purpose: Tracks Substrait as an optional interchange module.

capabilities.name: Device backends and DLPack
capabilities.notes: CPU is the required baseline; device identity, synchronization, transfers, and DLPack ownership are optional future features.

evidence.purpose: Tracks device support as optional while preserving a CPU baseline.

operations.name: Field and schema types
operations.rationale: Recursive fields, metadata, and nullability determine static validity and ABI representation.

operations.name: Nullable scalar type
operations.rationale: Nullability participates in assignment, branching, kernel typing, scalar extraction, and schema compatibility.

operations.name: Array type
operations.rationale: Array ownership, element nullability, calls, returns, indexing, and lowering require compiler knowledge.

operations.name: Series and chunked-array type
operations.rationale: Series is Arx's public typed chunked-column value and must carry ownership and chunking semantics.

operations.name: RecordBatch type
operations.rationale: A batch schema and row count are part of its static and native value contract.

operations.name: DataFrame and table type
operations.rationale: DataFrame remains the Arx-native table surface; the Arrow Table handle is an implementation detail.

operations.name: Dense tensor type
operations.rationale: Element type, rank, shape, strides, mutability, and device determine static safety and lowering.

operations.name: Batch stream type
operations.rationale: EOF, close, cancellation, iteration, and element ownership require compiler-visible resource semantics.

operations.name: Dataset and scanner handle types
operations.rationale: Handle and expression types are builtin for schema safety; orchestration remains in stdlib.dataset.

operations.name: Execution plan type
operations.rationale: Plan schemas, ownership, and execution state are compiler-visible while plan construction is library-oriented.

operations.name: Execution context type
operations.rationale: Memory pools, cancellation, limits, and thread policy need an opaque builtin value but not ambient syntax.

operations.name: Recoverable result and data error types
operations.rationale: Fallible native operations need typed success and error control flow without Python exceptions or unchecked output slots.

operations.name: Array literals and builders
operations.rationale: Construction resolves element type, validity, allocation, partial failure cleanup, and result ownership.

operations.name: Series construction
operations.rationale: Chunk compatibility and result ownership must be checked before native construction.

operations.name: RecordBatch construction
operations.rationale: Schema and equal-length validation are static when possible and use one native owning constructor.

operations.name: DataFrame construction
operations.rationale: The existing native literal syntax remains builtin and gains the canonical schema and ownership model.

operations.name: Tensor literals and views
operations.rationale: Shape, strides, offset, owner lifetime, mutability, and overflow need semantic and lowering support.

operations.name: Length, row count, and shape queries
operations.rationale: These are universal safe collection queries with checked i64 results and natural language syntax.

operations.name: Indexing and scalar extraction
operations.rationale: Bounds, scalar type, null validity, and view ownership must be proven or checked by the compiler.

operations.name: Zero-copy slicing
operations.rationale: Slicing creates borrowed or shared views whose bounds and owner lifetime need compiler support.

operations.name: Field and column projection
operations.rationale: Static schemas resolve projections during analysis; dynamic schemas must return checked dynamic values.

operations.name: Null inspection and validity
operations.rationale: Validity is part of core value semantics and must work without a library import.

operations.name: Checked casts
operations.rationale: The compiler resolves result type, overflow policy, nullability, and the exact native kernel.

operations.name: Collection and stream iteration
operations.rationale: Iteration controls scalar validity, chunk traversal, early exit, stream close, and cleanup.

operations.name: Chunk inspection and normalization
operations.rationale: Chunking changes representation, allocation, and ownership and must not be hidden in ordinary Arx code.

operations.name: Retain, release, move, and borrow primitives
operations.rationale: Ordinary Arx values get safe deterministic semantics; users do not balance native reference counts.

operations.name: Elementwise arithmetic
operations.surface: left + right, left - right, left * right, left / right
operations.rationale: Natural operators use typed kernel resolution and preserve Arx overflow and null rules.

operations.name: Elementwise comparisons
operations.rationale: Comparisons are native operators whose nullable Boolean result type is decided during analysis.

operations.name: Elementwise Boolean and Kleene logic
operations.surface: left and right, left or right, not value
operations.rationale: Boolean operators need language-defined three-valued behavior and typed kernel selection.

operations.name: Selection and conditional kernels
operations.surface: filter, take, drop_null, fill_null, if_else, coalesce
operations.rationale: Typed intrinsics back a discoverable domain module without adding keywords or an Arrow namespace.

operations.name: Aggregate kernels
operations.surface: sum, mean, min, max, count, any, all
operations.rationale: Aggregates need option types and typed scalar results but are better organized as domain functions.

operations.name: Sort, partition, and rank kernels
operations.rationale: Ordering policy and structured options belong in stdlib.compute over resolved intrinsic calls.

operations.name: Set and lookup kernels
operations.rationale: These are typed kernel families with nontrivial result schemas and options, not new syntax.

operations.name: String and binary kernels
operations.rationale: A typed registry can expose the long-tail kernel family without parser special cases.

operations.name: Temporal kernels
operations.surface: year, month, day, strftime, strptime, assume_timezone
operations.rationale: Units, timezones, formats, and result types are resolved by builtins and organized in stdlib.compute.

operations.name: Nested and encoding kernels
operations.rationale: Recursive result typing needs intrinsic metadata while the function families stay out of ambient syntax.

operations.name: Cumulative, sliding, and vector kernels
operations.rationale: Long-tail analytics use the same typed registry and execution context without becoming compiler syntax.

operations.name: Compute option values
operations.rationale: Closed typed option records are compiler-known declarations exposed through the compute facade.

operations.name: IPC stream and file I/O
operations.rationale: I/O needs policy and options, while native intrinsics retain ownership and status handling.

operations.name: CSV and JSON I/O
operations.rationale: Format options and streaming policy belong in stdlib.io over optional native runtime features.

operations.name: Parquet I/O
operations.rationale: Projection, row groups, codecs, and pushdown are library policy backed by typed native primitives.

operations.name: Filesystem and URI operations
operations.rationale: Filesystem selection and credentials are policy-heavy and feature-gated rather than ambient language behavior.

operations.name: Dataset discovery and opening
operations.rationale: Dataset orchestration is a domain API while schema and native handles remain compiler builtins.

operations.name: Scanner construction and execution
operations.rationale: Typed expressions and schemas are builtins; scan planning and execution form a composable library API.

operations.name: Fragments and partitioning
operations.rationale: These domain operations expose typed handles and metadata without adding core syntax.

operations.name: Acero plan composition and execution
operations.surface: source, project, filter, aggregate, join, order_by, sink
operations.rationale: A focused typed plan API composes runtime primitives without turning Arx into a separate query engine.

operations.name: Arrow C Data import and export
operations.rationale: The stable interchange ABI is available to bridges, but ordinary Arx code should use safe native values.

operations.name: Arrow C Stream import and export
operations.rationale: The callback ABI stays behind safe Stream ownership, EOF, cancellation, and close semantics.

operations.name: PyArrow conversion
operations.rationale: Python conversion belongs to ArxPy and must not appear in native Arx execution or the language namespace.

operations.name: Flight clients and servers
operations.rationale: RPC dependencies are optional and capability-named rather than nested below an Arrow namespace.

operations.name: Substrait import and export
operations.rationale: Plan interchange is optional and named for Substrait, with compiler checks around unsupported extensions.

operations.name: DLPack and device adapters
operations.rationale: Device dependencies and synchronization stay optional while compiler-known ownership prevents unsafe transfer.

modules.rationale: These types and containers define Arx's native data model and are compiler builtins rather than an imported library.
CPU dense and sparse types are language containers; non-CPU device execution remains separately optional.
Arx preserves registered extension identity and metadata but executes only extensions with explicit typed registrations.
The C Data and C Stream layouts are stable bridge ABIs hidden behind safe Arx values.
Common operations are builtin operators while the typed long-tail registry is exposed through stdlib.compute.
Focused plan composition is a dataset library surface backed by compiler-known schemas and handles.
Arrow stream and file primitives implement public stdlib.io operations but are not a separate Arx module.
IPC stream and file APIs are required native I/O with typed options and Stream ownership.
CSV readers and writers are required stdlib.io capabilities activated only when used.
JSON readers are required stdlib.io capabilities with explicit schema and resource policies.
Parquet is a required columnar format but remains an independently linked runtime feature.
Encryption adds crypto and credential policy and is excluded from the mandatory runtime payload.
Geospatial logical metadata is preserved by core Parquet and interpreted only by an optional typed feature.
Local files and URIs are required for I/O and datasets without adding cloud dependencies.
Provider SDKs, credentials, and platform dependencies ship only in the cloud companion runtime.
Dataset, fragment, and scanner orchestration is a required domain facade over builtin typed handles.
RPC, TLS, and authentication dependencies are optional and named directly for the capability.
Flight SQL is an optional protocol API and does not make SQL a core Arx language feature.
Plan interchange is optional and accepted only for operations mapped to typed Arx primitives.
CPU remains mandatory; device memory, synchronization, and transfers require an optional runtime.
ORC is a useful optional format adapter but is not part of the required CSV, JSON, Parquet, and IPC baseline.
Framework-specific TensorFlow integration belongs in an external ecosystem package, not the native language core.
Arx already lowers typed operations through IRx and Arrow Compute; a second LLVM expression compiler is not supported.
C++-specific adapters may be used inside native bridges but are not stable Arx or C ABI surfaces.
Telemetry may instrument execution contexts but does not define language-visible data semantics.
Upstream test utilities and integration executables are development inputs, not shipped public APIs.
Implementation utilities and vendored dependencies inherit the feature that uses them and have no public Arx identity.
Python conversion belongs to ArxPy tests and adapters and is never a dependency of native Arx execution.

modules.upstream: Arrow C++ benchmarks, examples, fuzzers, and tools
modules.rationale: Upstream developer programs inform Arx tests but are not distributable language or standard-library APIs.
